# criblio_search_dataset_intelligence (Resource)

SearchDatasetIntelligence Resource

Enables intelligence for an existing Search dataset. Creating the resource starts an asynchronous analysis; Terraform records the returned generation status without waiting for completion. Refresh state to read the latest status and generated Markdown. A `partial` or `failed` run remains managed and is not automatically retried.

AI and agentic Search must be enabled, AI consent accepted, and the caller must have read and maintainer access to the dataset. Built-in datasets require Search admin privileges to manage intelligence.

Destroying the resource removes the saved intelligence without deleting the dataset. To disable intelligence conditionally, use `count` or `for_each`. To regenerate it explicitly, run `terraform apply -replace=criblio_search_dataset_intelligence.example`. Import adopts existing intelligence without starting another analysis. Generated content and lifecycle metadata are read-only.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The dataset must already exist; reference criblio_search_dataset.<name>.id
# when Terraform manages it. Requires agentic Search and accepted AI consent.
resource "criblio_search_dataset_intelligence" "example" {
  dataset_id = "application_logs"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tools/codegen -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dataset_id` (String) ID of the existing Search dataset. Changing it replaces the intelligence resource.

### Read-Only

- `content` (String) Generated Markdown content, available when analysis has produced output.
- `failure_reason` (String) Failure details when analysis is partial or failed.
- `generated_at` (Integer) Generation start time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
- `status` (String) Generation status: processing, complete, partial, or failed.
- `updated_at` (Integer) Last manual edit time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, when present.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = criblio_search_dataset_intelligence.my_criblio_search_dataset_intelligence
  id = "example"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import criblio_search_dataset_intelligence.my_criblio_search_dataset_intelligence "example"
```
